question_text: Was the US Air Force's Cloud One cloud platform hacked?
answer_text: Reported as a hack. Reuters, NBC News and Federal News Network, each citing their own unnamed sources, say hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's main cloud platform. The Air Force has not confirmed or denied it on the record.
label: Reported

question_text: What did the hackers reach in Cloud One, and was any data taken?
what_would_settle_it: The Air Force or another official source, on the record, saying what was accessed and whether data was taken.

question_text: When did the Cloud One intrusion happen?
what_would_settle_it: An official account of when the intrusion began and when it was found; the outlets' sources so far disagree.

question_text: Who was behind the Cloud One breach?
what_would_settle_it: A US government attribution, or a named independent analysis.

question_text: Is Cloud One working normally again?
what_would_settle_it: The Air Force or a credible outlet saying the paused work and blocked updates have resumed.

question_text: Did AI-powered hackers break into Cloud One?
answer_text: Nobody has shown that. One of Reuters' sources says the intruders exploited a software flaw, but no source says how it was found or whether AI tools were used.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: An official or a named investigation describing how the intruders got in.

question_text: Is the Cloud One hack linked to the FBI, Treasury and other recent federal hacks?
answer_text: No source has linked them. Reuters lists the other recent incidents as background only, and nobody has named who was behind Cloud One.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: A government statement or named investigation tying the incidents to the same intruders.
